verdict.reasoning: Patient reports feeling breathless and right-sided back pain when breathing deeply: "Feeling very sort of breathless recently... whenever I like. Breathe deeply, it sort of catches in the right hand side of my back." Duration is one day: "Just. Just a day, really."
Patient reports subjective fever and two episodes of hemoptysis: "I've got a bit of a slight fever and, well, I coughed up a bit of blood on two occasions."

Patient describes feeling heart beating, fatigue, reduced exercise tolerance, and difficulty with daily activities for a couple of weeks: "I sort of feel my heart beating... I've been feeling a bit like a bit tired at work... exercising has been a bit difficult because I've been feeling tired and... Performing daily activities has been a bit harder than usual." Duration: "Only for a couple of weeks or so." The doctor clarifies feeling heart beating as likely faster: "you can feel your heart kind of beating a bit faster, you think, than normal?"
Patient confirms SLE: Doctor asks why methotrexate is taken, patient replies "I've got sle."
Medication and timing are stated: "Yeah. Methotrexate..." and to "When was the last time you had methotrexate?" Patient: "This morning."

No drug allergies reported: Doctor asks "do you have any allergies to any medication?" Patient: "No." Later doctor asks about antibiotic allergies: "Do you have any allergies to any antibiotics?" Patient: "No."
No family history of clots: Doctor: "Anyone in the family have that?" (re clots in legs or lungs). Patient: "No."
Smoking status: Doctor: "do you smoke at all?" Patient: "No."
Occupation: "What do you work as?" Patient: "I work in an office. Just a desk job."
Living situation: "And do you live alone?" Patient: "Yes." "In a flat or a house?" Patient: "Flat."
Pet ownership: "Do you have any pets?" Patient: "Cats?" Doctor: "A cat. Okay."
Travel: Doctor: "Have you been on any long haul flight recently?" Patient: "No. No."

Pulse rate and regularity: Doctor has patient count radial pulse; concludes, "that was about 11 or 12. So that would make your heart rate about 66 to 74. That's okay." Patient confirms feeling a regular pulse earlier: "I've got it."

Doctor demonstrates capillary refill and has patient perform it but does not explicitly describe the result as brisk or normal in words; only says "Okay, perfect. That's great." No explicit documentation of "brisk" capillary refill.

The doctor visually examines the throat via video and says "Perfect. Thank you for that. Excellent." but does not explicitly state that the oropharynx appears normal; describing it as normal is an inferred positive finding not directly stated.
Cervical lymph nodes: Doctor instructs self-palpation; patient: "No, they feel pretty normal to me." Doctor accepts this without contradiction, supporting that nodes are not enlarged on self-exam.

Doctor says it "sounds like you might have a chest infection" and that they need to assess for pneumonia vs chest infection; pulmonary embolism is only indirectly screened by questions about flights and clots, but PE is never explicitly mentioned as a differential to be ruled out. The full statement "pneumonia versus pulmonary embolism to be ruled out" is not in the transcript.

Subjective fever is acknowledged in history, but there is no separate assessment item labeled or discussed specifically as a distinct problem; doctor speaks of chest infection and general illness, not fever as its own assessment.

Fatigue is elicited in history, but the doctor does not discuss it etiologically (e.g., relation to current illness vs SLE vs methotrexate). The attribution "possibly related to the current illness or to SLE or methotrexate use" is not mentioned.

Same-day in-person review with vitals and chest exam is planned: "we'll arrange for you to get reviewed in a clinic today... listen to your chest and check your blood pressure and to recheck your pulse as well. Just make sure. Check your temperature, make sure all those parameters are okay."

Doctor mentions possible need for antibiotic and later possible follow-up chest X-ray: "we may end up having to do a follow up chest X ray if things don't settle down" but does not mention initial chest X-ray, blood tests, sputum culture, or explicit PE assessment if exam is concerning.

Doctor anticipates empiric antibiotics after assessment: "You may well need an antibiotic... I'm not going to prescribe anything for you now because I think you need to have that basic assessment first... that's what I would predict the next step might be."
The transcript does not contain explicit safety-net advice about specific red-flag symptoms like worsening breathlessness, increased hemoptysis, or high fever; these are not stated.

Doctor states: "I'm going to leave the number in the notes for this appointment for you to ring our support team and then they will book you in for a face to face appointment... today." indicating provision of support team contact for same-day booking.
